Pete Alonso regression is already showing in Year 1 of that 5-year, $155M deal. 

2nd-lowest SLG of his career (.463) — basically matching his career low of .459

2nd-lowest OPS of his career (.808)

Career-low ISO (.213)

2nd-highest BABIP of his career (.293) 

3rd-lowest wOBA of his career (.351)

3rd-highest K% of his career (24.7)

2nd-highest Whiff% of his career (26.9)

2nd-lowest contact% of his career (74.7)

Bat speed by year:
2023: 75.7 mph (92nd)
2024: 75.2 mph (91st)
2025: 75.2 mph (89th)
2026: 74.6 mph (77th)

Steady drop, already out of the elite range, and the lowest FastSwing% of his career under 50% for the first time in his career (47.8%)

This is exactly why locking him up for five years at $155M was not the right move. The Mets were 100% right about letting Pete Alonso walk and he wasn't changing what happened this season!!!!!
